clinician.trajectory_summary: 60-year-old man with HIV and prior Hodgkin's lymphoma presenting with altered mental status and pancytopenia. Physical exam showed bilateral cervical and inguinal lymphadenopathy. Initial labs revealed pancytopenia, electrolyte disturbances, AKI, and lactic acidosis. Imaging included non-contrast CT head negative for acute lesions, chest X-ray showing right lung base pneumonia, and CT abdomen demonstrating moderate splenomegaly and multiple enlarged lymph nodes including a large right common iliac node. Blood cultures grew MRSA. Lymph node biopsy pathology revealed fibrinoid necrosis and atypical lymphocytes, supporting grade III LyG diagnosis. Confirmation was limited by lack of documented immunohistochemical and detailed pulmonary CT findings.
